passages.text: On hearing this report, King Hezekiah tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and entered the house of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
King Hezekiah heard the report.
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
He tore his clothes.
He put on sackcloth.
He entered the house of the LORD.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י כִּשְׁמֹ֙עַ֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ וַיִּקְרַ֖ע אֶת־ בְּגָדָ֑יו וַיִּתְכַּ֣ס בַּשָּׂ֔ק וַיָּבֹ֖א בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: And he sent Eliakim the palace administrator, Shebna the scribe, and the leading priests, all wearing sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz to tell him, “This is what Hezekiah says: Today is a day of distress, rebuke, and disgrace; for children have come to the point of birth, but there is no strength to deliver them.
passages.sermon:
King Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Hezekiah sent a group of men to the prophet Isaiah.
He sent Eliakim, who managed the palace.
He sent Shebna, who was the scribe.
He sent the leading priests.
All of them wore sackcloth.
They went to Isaiah, the son of Amoz.
Isaiah was a prophet.
The men spoke to Isaiah.
They gave him a message from Hezekiah.
Hezekiah said, “Today is a day of distress.
Today is a day of rebuke.
Today is a day of disgrace.
Children have come to the point of birth.
But there is no strength to deliver them.”
passages.original: וַ֠יִּשְׁלַח אֶת־ אֶלְיָקִ֨ים אֲשֶׁר־ עַל־ הַבַּ֜יִת וְאֵ֣ת׀ שֶׁבְנָ֣א הַסּוֹפֵ֗ר וְאֵת֙ זִקְנֵ֣י הַכֹּהֲנִ֔ים מִתְכַּסִּ֖ים בַּשַּׂקִּ֑ים אֶל־ יְשַֽׁעְיָ֥הוּ בֶן־ אָמ֖וֹץ הַנָּבִֽיא׃ וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ יוֹם־ צָרָ֧ה וְתוֹכֵחָ֛ה וּנְאָצָ֖ה הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּ֣י בָ֤אוּ בָנִים֙ עַד־ מַשְׁבֵּ֔ר וְכֹ֥חַ אַ֖יִן לְלֵדָֽה׃

passages.text: Perhaps the LORD your God will hear the words of the Rabshakeh, whom his master the king of Assyria has sent to defy the living God, and He will rebuke him for the words that the LORD your God has heard. Therefore lift up a prayer for the remnant that still survives.”
passages.sermon:
The king of Assyria sent his official, the Rabshakeh, to speak against the living God.
The Rabshakeh spoke words of defiance against God.
The king of Assyria is the Rabshakeh’s master.
Perhaps the LORD your God will hear the words of the Rabshakeh.
The LORD is the living God.
The Rabshakeh has insulted God.
Perhaps the LORD your God will rebuke the Rabshakeh for these words.
The LORD your God has heard these words.
Pray for the people who remain.
These people are the remnant that still survives.
passages.original: אוּלַ֡י יִשְׁמַע֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ אֵ֣ת׀ דִּבְרֵ֣י רַב־ שָׁקֵ֗ה אֲשֶׁר֩ שְׁלָח֨וֹ מֶֽלֶךְ־ אַשּׁ֤וּר׀ אֲדֹנָיו֙ לְחָרֵף֙ אֱלֹהִ֣ים חַ֔י וְהוֹכִ֙יחַ֙ בַּדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמַ֖ע יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ וְנָשָׂ֣אתָ תְפִלָּ֔ה בְּעַ֥ד הַשְּׁאֵרִ֖ית הַנִּמְצָאָֽה׃

passages.text: So the servants of King Hezekiah went to Isaiah, who replied, “Tell your master that this is what the LORD says: ‘Do not be afraid of the words you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed Me.
passages.sermon:
King Hezekiah had servants.
These servants went to Isaiah.
Isaiah was a prophet.
Isaiah spoke to the servants.
Isaiah said, “Tell your master this message.
The LORD says this.
Do not be afraid.
You have heard certain words.
The servants of the king of Assyria spoke these words.
They have blasphemed Me, the LORD, with these words.”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֗אוּ עַבְדֵ֛י הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ אֶל־ יְשַׁעְיָֽהוּ׃ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם֙ יְשַֽׁעְיָ֔הוּ כֹּ֥ה תֹאמְר֖וּן אֶל־ אֲדֹנֵיכֶ֑ם כֹּ֣ה׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אַל־ תִּירָא֙ מִפְּנֵ֤י הַדְּבָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁמַ֔עְתָּ אֲשֶׁ֧ר גִּדְּפ֛וּ נַעֲרֵ֥י מֶלֶךְ־ אַשּׁ֖וּר אוֹתִֽי׃

passages.text: Behold, I will put a spirit in him so that he will hear a rumor and return to his own land, where I will cause him to fall by the sword.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is speaking about the king of Assyria.
The LORD says, “I will act against him.
I will put a spirit in him.
He will hear a rumor.
He will return to his own land.
I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land.”
passages.original: הִנְנִ֨י נוֹתֵ֥ן בּוֹ֙ ר֔וּחַ וְשָׁמַ֥ע שְׁמוּעָ֖ה וְשָׁ֣ב אֶל־ אַרְצ֑וֹ וְהִפַּלְתִּ֥יו בַּחֶ֖רֶב בְּאַרְצֽוֹ׃

passages.text: When the Rabshakeh heard that the king of Assyria had left Lachish, he withdrew and found the king fighting against Libnah.
passages.sermon:
The Rabshakeh was a high official of the king of Assyria.
He heard news about the king of Assyria.
He learned that the king had left Lachish.
The Rabshakeh left his current place.
He went to find the king of Assyria.
He found the king of Assyria at Libnah.
The king of Assyria was fighting against Libnah.
passages.original: וַיָּ֙שָׁב֙ רַב־ שָׁקֵ֔ה וַיִּמְצָא֙ אֶת־ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר נִלְחָ֖ם עַל־ לִבְנָ֑ה כִּ֣י שָׁמַ֔ע כִּ֥י נָסַ֖ע מִלָּכִֽישׁ׃

passages.text: Now Sennacherib had been warned about Tirhakah king of Cush: “He has set out to fight against you.” On hearing this, Sennacherib sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying, “Give this message to Hezekiah king of Judah: ‘Do not let your God, in whom you trust, deceive you by saying that Jerusalem will not be delivered into the hand of the king of Assyria.
passages.sermon:
Sennacherib was the king of Assyria.
Sennacherib heard a report about Tirhakah.
Tirhakah was the king of Cush.
The report said, “Tirhakah has set out to fight against you.”
Sennacherib heard this news.
He sent messengers to Hezekiah.
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
The messengers brought a message for Hezekiah.
The message said, “Do not let your God deceive you.”
“You trust in your God.”
“Do not believe that Jerusalem will not be handed over to the king of Assyria.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֗ע עַל־ תִּרְהָ֤קָה מֶֽלֶךְ־ כּוּשׁ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יָצָ֖א לְהִלָּחֵ֣ם אִתָּ֑ךְ וַיִּשְׁמַע֙ וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל־ חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לֵאמֹֽר׃ כֹּ֣ה תֹאמְר֗וּן אֶל־ חִזְקִיָּ֤הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אַל־ יַשִּֽׁאֲךָ֣ אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתָּ֛ה בּוֹטֵ֥חַ בּ֖וֹ לֵאמֹ֑ר לֹ֤א תִנָּתֵן֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם בְּיַ֖ד מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃

passages.text: Surely you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the other countries, devoting them to destruction. Will you then be spared?
passages.sermon:
The kings of Assyria attacked many countries.
They destroyed those countries completely.
You have heard about these things.
You are not different from those other countries.
You will not escape.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֣ה׀ אַתָּ֣ה שָׁמַ֗עְתָּ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשׂ֜וּ מַלְכֵ֥י אַשּׁ֛וּר לְכָל־ הָאֲרָצ֖וֹת לְהַחֲרִימָ֑ם וְאַתָּ֖ה תִּנָּצֵֽל׃

passages.text: Did the gods of the nations destroyed by my fathers rescue those nations—the gods of Gozan, Haran, and Rezeph, and of the people of Eden in Telassar?
passages.sermon:
The kings of Assyria destroyed many nations.
My fathers destroyed Gozan.
They destroyed Haran.
They destroyed Rezeph.
They destroyed the people of Eden in Telassar.
The nations worshiped their own gods.
Did the gods of these nations save them?
No, their gods did not rescue them.
passages.original: הַהִצִּ֨ילוּ אוֹתָ֜ם אֱלֹהֵ֤י הַגּוֹיִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִשְׁחִ֣יתוּ אֲבוֹתַ֔י אֶת־ גּוֹזָ֖ן וְאֶת־ חָרָ֑ן וְרֶ֥צֶף וּבְנֵי־ עֶ֖דֶן אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּתְלַשָּֽׂר׃

passages.text: Where are the kings of Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah?’ ”
passages.sermon:
The speaker is the king of Assyria.
He addresses the people of Judah.
He lists several cities and their kings.
He says, “Where is the king of Hamath?”
He says, “Where is the king of Arpad?”
He says, “Where is the king of Sepharvaim?”
He says, “Where is the king of Hena?”
He says, “Where is the king of Ivvah?”
He implies these kings are gone.
He suggests these cities have fallen.
He warns Judah by reminding them of these lost kings.
passages.original: אַיֵּ֤ה מֶֽלֶךְ־ חֲמָת֙ וּמֶ֣לֶךְ אַרְפָּ֔ד וּמֶ֖לֶךְ לָעִ֣יר סְפַרְוָ֑יִם הֵנַ֖ע וְעִוָּֽה׃

passages.text: So Hezekiah received the letter from the messengers, read it, and went up to the house of the LORD and spread it out before the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Messengers brought a letter to Hezekiah.
Hezekiah took the letter from the messengers.
Hezekiah read the letter.
Hezekiah went up to the house of the LORD.
Hezekiah spread the letter out before the LORD.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֨ח חִזְקִיָּ֧הוּ אֶת־ הַסְּפָרִ֛ים מִיַּ֥ד הַמַּלְאָכִ֖ים וַיִּקְרָאֵ֑הוּ וַיַּ֙עַל֙ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה וַיִּפְרְשֵׂ֥הוּ חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: And Hezekiah prayed to the LORD: “O LORD of Hosts, God of Israel, enthroned above the cherubim, You alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made the heavens and the earth.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Hezekiah prayed to the LORD.
Hezekiah said, “LORD of Hosts, you are the God of Israel.
You sit above the cherubim.
You alone are God.
You rule over all the kingdoms of the earth.
You made the heavens.
You made the earth.”
passages.original: וַיִּתְפַּלֵּל֙ חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ אֶל־ יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יֹשֵׁ֣ב הַכְּרֻבִ֔ים אַתָּה־ ה֤וּא הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ לְבַדְּךָ֔ לְכֹ֖ל מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הָאָ֑רֶץ אַתָּ֣ה עָשִׂ֔יתָ אֶת־ הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וְאֶת־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: Incline Your ear, O LORD, and hear; open Your eyes, O LORD, and see. Listen to all the words that Sennacherib has sent to defy the living God.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was king of Judah.
Hezekiah prayed to the LORD.
Hezekiah spoke to the LORD, the God of Israel.
Hezekiah said, "LORD, incline Your ear."
Hezekiah asked, "Hear me."
Hezekiah said, "LORD, open Your eyes."
Hezekiah asked, "See what is happening."
Hezekiah said, "Listen to all the words of Sennacherib."
Sennacherib was king of Assyria.
Sennacherib sent words to defy the living God.
Hezekiah asked the LORD to hear and see Sennacherib's words against God.
passages.original: הַטֵּ֨ה יְהוָ֤ה׀ אָזְנְךָ֙ וּֽשְׁמָ֔ע פְּקַ֧ח יְהוָ֛ה עֵינֶ֖ךָ וּרְאֵ֑ה וּשְׁמַ֗ע אֵ֚ת כָּל־ דִּבְרֵ֣י סַנְחֵרִ֔יב אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁלַ֔ח לְחָרֵ֖ף אֱלֹהִ֥ים חָֽי׃

passages.text: Truly, O LORD, the kings of Assyria have laid waste all these countries and their lands.
passages.sermon: The kings of Assyria destroyed many countries.\r\nThey ruined the lands of those countries.\r\nThis is true, O LORD.
passages.original: אָמְנָ֖ם יְהוָ֑ה הֶחֱרִ֜יבוּ מַלְכֵ֥י אַשּׁ֛וּר אֶת־ כָּל־ הָאֲרָצ֖וֹת וְאֶת־ אַרְצָֽם׃

passages.text: They have cast their gods into the fire and destroyed them, for they were not gods, but only wood and stone—the work of human hands.
passages.sermon:
The kings of Assyria took the gods of the nations.
They threw these gods into the fire.
These gods were not real gods.
They were only objects made by people.
People made them from wood and stone.
The kings of Assyria destroyed these false gods.
passages.original: וְנָתֹ֥ן אֶת־ אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֖ם בָּאֵ֑שׁ כִּי֩ לֹ֨א אֱלֹהִ֜ים הֵ֗מָּה כִּ֣י אִם־ מַעֲשֵׂ֧ה יְדֵֽי־ אָדָ֛ם עֵ֥ץ וָאֶ֖בֶן וַֽיְאַבְּדֽוּם׃

passages.text: And now, O LORD our God, save us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that You alone, O LORD, are God.”
passages.sermon:
The people of Judah faced a great threat from the king of Assyria.
Hezekiah prayed to the LORD, the God of Israel.
Hezekiah said, “LORD our God, save us from his hand.
Rescue us from the power of the king of Assyria.
Then all the kingdoms of the earth will know this truth.
You alone, LORD, are God.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּה֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ הוֹשִׁיעֵ֖נוּ מִיָד֑וֹ וְיֵֽדְעוּ֙ כָּל־ מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּֽי־ אַתָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה לְבַדֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent a message to Hezekiah: “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Because you have prayed to Me concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria, this is the word that the LORD has spoken against him: ‘The Virgin Daughter of Zion despises you and mocks you; the Daughter of Jerusalem shakes her head behind you.
passages.sermon:
Isaiah was a prophet.
Isaiah was the son of Amoz.
Isaiah sent a message to Hezekiah.
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Isaiah spoke for the LORD.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD said this message.
Hezekiah prayed to the LORD.
Hezekiah prayed about Sennacherib.
Sennacherib was the king of Assyria.
The LORD answered Hezekiah’s prayer.
The LORD spoke a word against Sennacherib.
The LORD said, “The Virgin Daughter of Zion despises you.”
The LORD said, “She mocks you.”
The LORD said, “The Daughter of Jerusalem shakes her head at you.”
She does this behind you.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ יְשַֽׁעְיָ֣הוּ בֶן־ אָמ֔וֹץ אֶל־ חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לֵאמֹ֑ר כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁר֙ הִתְפַּלַּ֣לְתָּ אֵלַ֔י אֶל־ סַנְחֵרִ֖יב מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃ זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁר־ דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה עָלָ֑יו בָּזָ֨ה לְךָ֜ לָעֲגָ֣ה לְךָ֗ בְּתוּלַת֙ בַּת־ צִיּ֔וֹן אַחֲרֶ֙יךָ֙ רֹ֣אשׁ הֵנִ֔יעָה בַּ֖ת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: Whom have you taunted and blasphemed? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted your eyes in pride? Against the Holy One of Israel!
passages.sermon:
Sennacherib is the king of Assyria.
Sennacherib has taunted and blasphemed someone.
Sennacherib has raised his voice against someone.
Sennacherib has lifted his eyes in pride against someone.
Sennacherib has done these things against the Holy One of Israel.
passages.original: אֶת־ מִ֤י חֵרַ֙פְתָּ֙ וְגִדַּ֔פְתָּ וְעַל־ מִ֖י הֲרִימ֣וֹתָה קּ֑וֹל וַתִּשָּׂ֥א מָר֛וֹם עֵינֶ֖יךָ אֶל־ קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: Through your servants you have taunted the Lord, and you have said: “With my many chariots I have ascended to the heights of the mountains, to the remote peaks of Lebanon. I have cut down its tallest cedars, the finest of its cypresses. I have reached its farthest heights, the densest of its forests.
passages.sermon:
Sennacherib is the king of Assyria.
Sennacherib has spoken against the Lord.
Sennacherib has used his servants to insult the Lord.
Sennacherib said, “I have many chariots.”
Sennacherib said, “I went up to the high mountains.”
Sennacherib said, “I reached the far places of Lebanon.”
Sennacherib said, “I cut down the tallest cedar trees.”
Sennacherib said, “I cut down the best cypress trees.”
Sennacherib said, “I entered the highest parts of the mountains.”
Sennacherib said, “I entered the thickest forests.”
passages.original: בְּיַ֣ד עֲבָדֶיךָ֮ חֵרַ֣פְתָּ׀ אֲדֹנָי֒ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר בְּרֹ֥ב רִכְבִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י עָלִ֛יתִי מְר֥וֹם הָרִ֖ים יַרְכְּתֵ֣י לְבָנ֑וֹן וְאֶכְרֹ֞ת קוֹמַ֤ת אֲרָזָיו֙ מִבְחַ֣ר בְּרֹשָׁ֔יו וְאָבוֹא֙ מְר֣וֹם קִצּ֔וֹ יַ֖עַר כַּרְמִלּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: I have dug wells and drunk foreign waters. With the soles of my feet I have dried up all the streams of Egypt.”
passages.sermon:
The speaker is a proud conqueror.
He says, “I have dug wells.
I have drunk water from foreign lands.
I have used the soles of my feet.
I have dried up all the streams of Egypt.”
passages.original: אֲנִ֥י קַ֖רְתִּי וְשָׁתִ֣יתִי מָ֑יִם וְאַחְרִב֙ בְּכַף־ פְּעָמַ֔י כֹּ֖ל יְאֹרֵ֥י מָצֽוֹר׃

passages.text: Have you not heard? Long ago I ordained it; in days of old I planned it. Now I have brought it to pass, that you should crush fortified cities into piles of rubble.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the proud king of Assyria.
God says, “Have you not heard?
I decided this long ago.
I planned it in ancient times.
Now I have made it happen.
You destroy strong cities.
You turn them into heaps of ruins.”
passages.original: הֲלֽוֹא־ שָׁמַ֤עְתָּ לְמֵֽרָחוֹק֙ אוֹתָ֣הּ עָשִׂ֔יתִי מִ֥ימֵי קֶ֖דֶם וִיצַרְתִּ֑יהָ עַתָּ֣ה הֲבֵאתִ֔יהָ וּתְהִ֗י לְהַשְׁא֛וֹת גַּלִּ֥ים נִצִּ֖ים עָרִ֥ים בְּצֻרֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Therefore their inhabitants, devoid of power, are dismayed and ashamed. They are like plants in the field, tender green shoots, grass on the rooftops, scorched before it is grown.
passages.sermon:
The people who lived in those cities had no strength.
They felt afraid.
They felt ashamed.
They were like grass in a field.
They were like young green plants.
They were like grass that grows on rooftops.
They dried up before they could grow tall.
passages.original: וְיֹֽשְׁבֵיהֶן֙ קִצְרֵי־ יָ֔ד חַ֖תּוּ וָבֹ֑שׁוּ הָי֞וּ עֵ֤שֶׂב שָׂדֶה֙ וִ֣ירַק דֶּ֔שֶׁא חֲצִ֣יר גַּגּ֔וֹת וּשְׁדֵמָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֥י קָמָֽה׃

passages.text: But I know your sitting down, your going out and coming in, and your raging against Me.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the king of Assyria.
God knows everything the king does.
God knows when the king sits down.
God knows when the king goes out.
God knows when the king comes in.
God knows the king’s anger against Him.
passages.original: וְשִׁבְתְּךָ֛ וְצֵאתְךָ֥ וּבוֹאֲךָ֖ יָדָ֑עְתִּי וְאֵ֖ת הִֽתְרַגֶּזְךָ֥ אֵלָֽי׃

passages.text: Because your rage and arrogance against Me have reached My ears, I will put My hook in your nose and My bit in your mouth; I will send you back the way you came.’
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the enemy of Judah.
You have raged against Me.
You have shown arrogance toward Me.
Your rage and arrogance have reached My ears.
I will act against you.
I will put My hook in your nose.
I will put My bit in your mouth.
I will force you to return.
You will go back the way you came.
passages.original: יַ֚עַן הִתְרַגֶּזְךָ֣ אֵלַ֔י וְשַׁאֲנַנְךָ֖ עָלָ֣ה בְאָזְנָ֑י וְשַׂמְתִּ֨י חַחִ֜י בְּאַפֶּ֗ךָ וּמִתְגִּי֙ בִּשְׂפָתֶ֔יךָ וַהֲשִׁ֣יבֹתִ֔יךָ בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֥אתָ בָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: And this will be a sign to you, O Hezekiah: This year you will eat what grows on its own, and in the second year what springs from the same. But in the third year you will sow and reap; you will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to King Hezekiah.
God gave a sign to Hezekiah.
This year, you will eat food that grows by itself.
Next year, you will eat what grows from the same plants.
In the third year, you will plant seeds.
You will gather the harvest.
You will plant vineyards.
You will eat the fruit from the vineyards.
passages.original: וְזֶה־ לְּךָ֣ הָא֔וֹת אָכ֤וֹל הַשָּׁנָה֙ סָפִ֔יחַ וּבַשָּׁנָ֥ה הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית שָׁחִ֑יס וּבַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֗ית זִרְע֧וּ וְקִצְר֛וּ וְנִטְע֥וּ כְרָמִ֖ים וְאָכוֹל פִרְיָֽם׃

passages.text: And the surviving remnant of the house of Judah will again take root below and bear fruit above.
passages.sermon: The house of Judah has a surviving remnant.\r\nThis remnant will take root below.\r\nThis remnant will bear fruit above.
passages.original: וְיָ֨סְפָ֜ה פְּלֵיטַ֧ת בֵּית־ יְהוּדָ֛ה הַנִּשְׁאָרָ֖ה שֹׁ֣רֶשׁ לְמָ֑טָּה וְעָשָׂ֥ה פְרִ֖י לְמָֽעְלָה׃

passages.text: For a remnant will go forth from Jerusalem, and survivors from Mount Zion. The zeal of the LORD of Hosts will accomplish this.
passages.sermon:
A remnant will leave Jerusalem.
Survivors will come from Mount Zion.
The LORD of Hosts is powerful.
His zeal will make this happen.
passages.original: כִּ֤י מִירֽוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ תֵּצֵ֣א שְׁאֵרִ֔ית וּפְלֵיטָ֖ה מֵהַ֣ר צִיּ֑וֹן קִנְאַ֛ת יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת תַּֽעֲשֶׂה־ זֹּֽאת׃ס

passages.text: So this is what the LORD says about the king of Assyria: ‘He will not enter this city or shoot an arrow into it. He will not come before it with a shield or build up a siege ramp against it.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke about the king of Assyria.
The LORD said these words.
The king of Assyria will not enter this city.
He will not shoot an arrow into this city.
He will not come against this city with a shield.
He will not build a siege ramp against this city.
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר לֹ֤א יָבוֹא֙ אֶל־ הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את וְלֹֽא־ יוֹרֶ֥ה שָׁ֖ם חֵ֑ץ וְלֹֽא־ יְקַדְּמֶ֣נָּה מָגֵ֔ן וְלֹֽא־ יִשְׁפֹּ֥ךְ עֳלֶ֖יהָ סֹלְלָֽה׃

passages.text: He will go back the way he came, and he will not enter this city,’ declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD refers to the king of Assyria.
The king of Assyria will return by the same way he came.
The king of Assyria will not enter this city.
The LORD has declared this.
passages.original: בַּדֶּ֥רֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֖א בָּ֣הּ יָשׁ֑וּב וְאֶל־ הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֛את לֹ֥א יָב֖וֹא נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: ‘I will defend this city and save it for My own sake and for the sake of My servant David.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is speaking.
The LORD promises to defend this city.
The LORD will save this city.
The LORD acts for His own sake.
The LORD also acts for the sake of His servant David.
passages.original: וְגַנּוֹתִ֛י עַל־ הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֖את לְהֽוֹשִׁיעָ֑הּ לְמַֽעֲנִ֔י וּלְמַ֖עַן דָּוִ֥ד עַבְדִּֽי׃ס

passages.text: Then the angel of the LORD went out and struck down 185,000 men in the camp of the Assyrians. When the people got up the next morning, there were all the dead bodies!
passages.sermon:
The angel of the LORD went out.
The angel of the LORD struck down 185,000 men.
These men were in the camp of the Assyrians.
The people got up the next morning.
They saw all the dead bodies.
passages.original: וַיֵּצֵ֣א׀ מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֗ה וַיַּכֶּה֙ בְּמַחֲנֵ֣ה אַשּׁ֔וּר מֵאָ֛ה וּשְׁמֹנִ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה אָ֑לֶף וַיַּשְׁכִּ֣ימוּ בַבֹּ֔קֶר וְהִנֵּ֥ה כֻלָּ֖ם פְּגָרִ֥ים מֵתִֽים׃

passages.text: So Sennacherib king of Assyria broke camp and withdrew. He returned to Nineveh and stayed there.
passages.sermon:
Sennacherib was the king of Assyria.
He broke camp.
He left the area.
He returned to Nineveh.
He stayed in Nineveh.
passages.original: וַיִּסַּ֣ע וַיֵּ֔לֶךְ וַיָּ֖שָׁב סַנְחֵרִ֣יב מֶֽלֶךְ־ אַשּׁ֑וּר וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב בְּנִֽינְוֵֽה׃

passages.text: One day, while he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer put him to the sword and escaped to the land of Ararat. And his son Esar-haddon reigned in his place.
passages.sermon:
Sennacherib was the king of Assyria.
He went to the temple of his god Nisroch.
He worshiped there.
His sons were Adrammelech and Sharezer.
Adrammelech and Sharezer killed Sennacherib with a sword.
They escaped to the land of Ararat.
Esar-haddon was Sennacherib’s son.
Esar-haddon became king after Sennacherib.
passages.original: וַיְהִי֩ ה֨וּא מִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֜ה בֵּ֣ית׀ נִסְרֹ֣ךְ אֱלֹהָ֗יו וְֽאַדְרַמֶּ֨לֶךְ וְשַׂרְאֶ֤צֶר בָּנָיו֙ הִכֻּ֣הוּ בַחֶ֔רֶב וְהֵ֥מָּה נִמְלְט֖וּ אֶ֣רֶץ אֲרָרָ֑ט וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֵֽסַר־ חַדֹּ֥ן בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃ס
